items.title: Reclaiming the field: Mineral taxation, federalism and the MMDR (Amendment) Act 2026
items.summary: The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026 (the “ 2026 Act ”/” Act ”) introduces a significant shift in the fiscal framework governing India’s mineral sector. Coming shortly after the Supreme Court’s nine-judge Bench decision in Mineral Area Development Authority v. Steel Authority of India, (2024) 10 SCC 1 (MADA), the amendment seeks to clarify and, in important respects, reshape the limits within which States may impose levies connected with mineral rights and mineral-bearing land. The resulting questions of legislative competence, federalism and retrospectivity are likely to be closely tested before the courts. The amendment is the latest in a series of changes to India’s mineral regulatory framework. The 2015 amendment introduced auctions; the 2021 amendment liberalised captive production; and the 2023 and 2025 amendments opened critical minerals to greater private participation. The 2026 Act takes the next step by seeking to establish a more uniform fiscal framework for mineral development. Its significance, however, extends beyond taxation: it raises broader questions about the constitutional balance between Union regulation and State taxing powers. The MADA windfall In July 2024, Supreme Court in MADA case (supra) held, 8:1, that royalty under the MMDR Act is not a tax but a contractual payment to the lessor, and overruled the seven-judge decision in India Cement Ltd. v. State of Tamil Nadu (1990) 1 SCC 12 , which had been read for three decades as denying the States any power to impose levies referable to mineral rights. The majority located two distinct heads of State competence: Entry 50 of List II, which permits taxes on mineral rights “subject to any limitations imposed by Parliament by law relating to mineral development”, and Entry 49 of List II, the general power to tax lands, which the Court held could reach mineral-bearing land using mineral value or yield as the measure. Hon’ble Justice Nagarathna, dissenting, warned that a patchwork of State levies would fragment the national mineral market. A consequential order followed in August 2024. The Court declined to make its ruling purely prospective: States could recover dues from April 1, 2005, though interest and penalties on amounts predating July 25, 2024, were waived and payment was to be staggered over twelve years beginning April 1, 2026. For the mineral-rich States like Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal, this was a fiscal windfall

items.title: Police can't pick and choose which accused to arrest: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently observed that the police cannot selectively arrest some of the accused persons and the policy of picking and choosing persons to be taken into custody must be deprecated [Rajkumar v State (NCT of Delhi)] . Justice Girish Kathpalia said that the police must clearly state whether it wants to arrest a person or not. “Of course, the policy of the State to selectively arrest some of the accused persons cannot be approved. The police should clearly state as to whether they want to arrest an accused or not. The Court cannot direct the police to do or not to do so. Such kind of pick and choose in matter of arrest must be deprecated,” the Bench said. Justice Girish Kathpalia Delhi High Court The policy of the State to selectively arrest some of the accused persons cannot be approved... Such kind of pick and choose in matter of arrest must be deprecated. The Court made the observation while rejecting a bail application of one Rajkumar, an accused in a child trafficking case. According to the prosecution, Rajkumar and co-accused Gayatri had posed as a married couple to take an infant girl in adoption, subsequently selling her to co-accused Deepika, who sold the child further. The infant was the sixth girl child in the family of her biological parents. Rajkumar's counsel argued that his client had been falsely implicated merely for being Deepika's paternal uncle, and that the main accused, Dr Kulvinder Kaur, remains unarrested. After considering the case, the Court noted that the police failed to explain why Kulvinder Kaur was not arrested. It also observed that since Rajkumar does not have the custody of the child, it is likely that she has been sold away. Justice Kathpalia said that the role played by the “investigators in this case is highly appalling” since they have failed to recover the trafficked child even two years after the FIR was registered. Meanwhile, the police told the Court that co-accused Kulvinder Kaur would be arrested. The Court has now directed the Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) to take steps to recover the child and file a status report within four weeks. The Court has also sent its order to the DCP to consider its observations on selective arrests. Advocate Shrikant Sharma appeared for accused Rajkumar. [Read Order]

items.title: Collegium recommends Justice Krushna Ram Mohapatra as Chief Justice of Chhattisgarh High Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of Justice Krushna Ram Mohapatra , a judge of the Orissa High Court, as Chief Justice of the High Court of Chhattisgarh. The recommendation was made at a Collegium meeting held on August 6 and comes consequent upon the retirement of the incumbent Chief Justice Ramesh Sinha on September 4. If the Centre confirms the Collegium's recommendation, Justice Mohapatra will take charge as Chief Justice of the Chhattisgarh High Court following the incumbent's retirement. Justice Mohapatra worked as Additional Standing Counsel for the State as well as the Orissa Public Service Commission, and served as advocate for entities including Central Cooperative Banks Limited (Keonjhar), the National Institute of Open Schooling under the Ministry of HRD, Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited, and Bank of Baroda. He was elevated as a judge of the Orissa High Court on April 17, 2015 where he has been serving till date.

items.title: No basis to say homeless will be excluded from SIR: Delhi HC rejects PIL on persons displaced by demolition drives
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently observed that the apprehension that homeless persons will be excluded from the draft electoral roll published after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the national capital appeared to be without any basis. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia made the observation while dismissing a public interest litigation (PIL) petition seeking directions to the Election Commission of India (ECI) to establish a special facilitative mechanism for homeless persons and those displaced by demolition drives. "Having considered the submissions on behalf of learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner as well as learned Counsel for the ECI, we are of the considered opinion that the Manual already provide process for determination of the ordinary residence in accordance with the Representation of People Act for homeless persons as per Clause 8.5 of the Manual. Therefore, the apprehension of the petitioner that the homeless persons shall be excluded from the Draft Electoral Roll appears to be without any basis," the Court said. It added that any excluded elector remains free to file Form 6. "The Manual clearly provides that once the details are provided by homeless persons in Form 6, the BLO will visit the address given therein for more than one night to ascertain that the homeless person actually sleeps at the given place,” the Bench observed. It was argued this violated Article 326 of the Constitution and the ECI's own 2011 BLO Handbook, which recognises that homelessness is not a disqualification for enrolment. The ECI countered that clause 8.5 of the manual permits homeless and pavement dwellers without documentary proof of residence to enrol, provided a BLO verifies their presence at the given address over more than one night, with an additional safeguard requiring a statement on the person's birthplace and prior residence. items.title: Karnataka forms 6-member cabinet panel to review, recommend withdrawal of criminal cases
items.summary: The Karnataka government has constituted a 6-member cabinet sub-committee to examine pending criminal cases and recommend which ones may be considered for withdrawal. The committee headed by State Home Minister Priyank Kharge will comprise Health Minister UT Khader, Social Welfare Minister KH Muniyappa, Municipal Administration Minister HC Balakrishna, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda and Urban Development Department Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah. According to a press release issued by the Home Minister's office, the committee will examine the nature and background of each case, besides other relevant factors, before making its recommendations. The government has directed that the recommendations of the committee be made in accordance with the applicable rules governing withdrawal of criminal cases. The release further stated that the Home Department shall provide the necessary assistance to the cabinet sub-committee in accordance with Rule 13(5) of the Karnataka Government (Transaction of Business) Rules, 1977, and the circular issued by the department on March 15, 2025. The concerned departments have also been directed to provide the necessary assistance to the cabinet sub-committee in carrying out the review. The committee's recommendations will subsequently be placed before the government for consideration in accordance with the applicable legal and administrative framework.

items.title: Daiichi-Ranbaxy dispute: Delhi High Court orders forensic audit of Fortis share transactions
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has ordered a comprehensive forensic audit to trace the dissipation of Fortis Healthcare Limited (FHL) shares and other assets that were available to satisfy the arbitral award secured by Japanese pharmaceutical company Daiichi Sankyo against former Ranbaxy promoters Malvinder Mohan Singh and Shivinder Mohan Singh [Daichii Sankyo Vs Malvinder Mohan Singh]. Justice Subramonium Prasad appointed chartered accountancy firm S Ramanand Aiyar & Co as the forensic auditor and directed it to complete the exercise within six months. The Court said the audit would reconstruct the entire chain of transactions and identify the persons, companies, banks and financial institutions involved in the depletion of the shares. Justice Subramonium Prasad The dispute arose from Daiichi’s 2008 acquisition of Ranbaxy from the Singh brothers and allegations that they concealed US regulatory investigations. A Singapore tribunal awarded Daiichi ₹2,562 crore in 2016. While enforcing the award, Fortis shares, available for recovery, sharply declined despite court assurances. The Supreme Court later convicted the brothers of contempt of court and asked the Delhi High Court to consider forensic audits of transactions involving banks, financial institutions, FHL and RHT Health Trust in 2022. This direction led to the initiation of the current litigation. The Court noted that despite nearly a decade of enforcement proceedings, Daiichi has not received the amount awarded to it by the arbitral tribunal. “ It is tragic to note that even after such strong observations by the Indian Courts throughout the years, nothing has changed even today. Generations pass but decrees are not executed as the judgment debtor has several arrows up in his quiver to defeat the rights of a decree holder, ” the Court said. The Court recorded that the Singh brothers and their entities held 5.29 crore unencumbered FHL shares in September 2016. By December 2018, this had fallen to about 6.01 lakh shares. It found that around 5.23 crore unencumbered shares had been sold despite assurances given to the Court that sufficient assets would remain available to protect Daiichi’s interests. “ The Courts cannot be mere silent spectator and throw out their hands in vain and say nothing can be done. items.title: Decision by Rajasthan High Court acting Chief Justice SP Sharma to opt out of judicial work was voluntary
items.summary: The decision of Rajasthan High Court acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma to stop holding court was not the consequence of any intervention by or direction from the Supreme Court but was a voluntary decision taken by the judge himself in view of the controversy over his continuance as the acting Chief Justice. Sources aware of the developments confirmed to Bar & Bench that Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant received a communication sent by Justice Sharma to the Supreme Court administration. The CJI was holding court on Monday when Justice Sharma's communication reached the Registrar General of the Supreme Court. The CJI was apprised of the communication only after he returned to his chambers following court proceedings. In his communication, Justice Sharma conveyed that he was voluntarily stepping away from holding court in view of the controversy. The development came amid protests at the Rajasthan High Court with lawyers resorting to strike against Justice Sharma, demanding that he be divested of his charge as the acting Chief Justice and that a permanent Chief Justice be appointed to the High Court. The Rajasthan High Court Lawyers Association announced a complete strike till September 6 after an emergency general house meeting on Monday. EXCLUSIVE: Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta asks CJI Surya Kant to replace Rajasthan HC Acting Chief Justice for misusing office The protests by lawyers stemmed from allegations made by Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta against Justice Sharma. As first reported by Bar & Bench , Justice Mehta had written to the CJI Surya Kant alleging manipulation of case listings and misuse of administrative powers by Justice Sharma. The CJI subsequently said that the Collegium was examining the allegations and that Justice Sharma would be given an opportunity to respond before any conclusion was reached. These revelations triggered protests by lawyers, prompting Justice Sharma to step away from his role as acting Chief Justice . Pertinently, the Supreme Court Collegium on Monday evening recommended the appointment of Justice Sanjay K Agrawal of the Chhattisgarh High Court as the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court. This move is likely to address the immediate demand by the Rajasthan High Court bar. Exclusive: Supreme Court Collegium recommends Justice Sanjay K Agrawal as Rajasthan High Court Chief Justice

items.title: Collegium recommends Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as Jammu & Kashmir High Court Chief Justice
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati as Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Justice Bhati is currently a judge of the Rajasthan High Court. The decision to recommend his name for Chief Justice was taken by the collegium at a meeting held on August 31. If the Centre confirms the collegium's recommendation, Justice Bhati will take over as Chief Justice from Justice Sanjeev Kumar who has been serving as acting Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh since June 2. Justice Bhati was a lawyer practicing across several areas of law for nearly 25 before he was elevated to the bench of the Rajasthan High Court on November 16, 2016. As a lawyer, he served as a Additional Advocate General for the State and was elected as President of the High Court Lawyers Association at different points Justice Bhati's wife, Justice Nupur Bhati, was also elevated as a judge of the Rajasthan High Court in 2023.

items.title: Supreme Court Collegium recommends Justice AY Kogje as Chief Justice of Madhya Pradesh High Court
items.summary: Justice Alpesh Yeshvant Kogje from Gujarat High Court has been recommended for appointment as the Chief Justice of the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The recommendation was made by the Supreme Court Collegium in its meeting held on August 31. Justice Kogje is presently serving as a judge of the Gujarat High Court. Justice Kogje completed his B.Sc. in Chemistry in 1990 and earned his law degree from the Faculty of Law at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda in 1993. He joined the Bar in 1993. Throughout his career as counsel, he held several significant roles, including Additional Public Prosecutor from 2002 to 2007, Standing Counsel for the Central Excise and Customs Department, and Special Public Prosecutor for the Special Investigation Team (SIT), where he notably handled a large volume of important cases arising from the 2002 Godhra riots. He was elevated as an additional judge of the Gujarat High Court in April 2016. He was subsequently appointed as a permanent judge of the Gujarat High Court in March 2018. The Madhya Pradesh High Court is presently functioning with 38 judges while its sanctioned strength is 53. [Read Collegium Statement]

items.title: Exclusive: Supreme Court Collegium recommends Justice Sanjay K Agrawal as Rajasthan High Court Chief Justice
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of Justice Sanjay K Agrawal of the Chhattisgarh High Court as the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court, Bar & Bench has learnt. Significantly, the Collegium has also proposed that Justice Agrawal be immediately transferred to the Rajasthan High Court, pending his appointment as its Chief Justice. The move would mean that even if the process for his appointment as Chief Justice takes time, Justice Agrawal would join the Rajasthan High Court as its senior-most judge. Justice Agrawal is presently a judge of the Chhattisgarh High Court. He was elevated as an additional judge of that Court in September 2013 and made a permanent judge in March 2016. Before his elevation, he had served as the Advocate General of Chhattisgarh. The development assumes significance in the backdrop of the controversy surrounding the present acting Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court, Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma . Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta recently wrote to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant seeking Justice Sharma's transfer out of Rajasthan and appointment of a regular Chief Justice from another High Court. Justice Mehta levelled allegations concerning the exercise of administrative powers and case listings by Justice Sharma. The controversy also triggered protests by lawyers at both the Jaipur and Jodhpur benches of the Rajasthan High Court, with lawyers demanding that Justice Sharma be divested of his charge as acting Chief Justice. Justice Sharma later opted himself out of judicial work . A fresh roster finalised by him on Monday does not assign any regular judicial sitting to him from September 1 to September 5. Matters which were earlier assigned to his Bench have been allocated to other Benches. If the Central government clears the recommendation, Justice Agrawal will take over as the regular Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court. [Read Collegium Statement]

items.title: TN: Woman’s body chopped into seven parts, dumped in water tanks in three sacks
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The dismembered body of a 50-year-old woman who had been reported missing on August 22, was found packed in three sacks in two overhead water tanks of a house in Arisipalayam on Monday, August 31, in Tamil Nadu's Salem district. The deceased was identified as Thangamani, a resident of Balaji Colony in Thathanur in Mettupatti. She worked as a domestic worker at a house in Hasthampatti and had been reported missing at the Hasthampathi police station. The gruesome murder came to light after Ramesh (62), a temple priest residing in Arisipalayam, returned home with his wife Jamunarani and son Gautham after a two-day trip to Kumbakonam and Thanjavur. On opening a tap for domestic use, the family noticed a foul smell emanating from the water. According to reports, Ramesh and his son checked the two overhead water tanks on the terrace. They found sacks containing body parts in both tanks. One sack contained severed hands and legs, while another contained the severed head of a woman. Another sack containing the remaining body parts was also found. Police said the woman's body had been chopped into seven pieces and packed in the three sacks. The Pallapatti police were alerted and rushed to the spot. The three sacks were subsequently sent to Salem Government Hospital for postmortem examination. Police said the deceased had the name ‘Ganapathi’ tattooed on her arm. The body was later identified as that of Thangamani, based on a missing-person complaint registered with the Hasthampathi police. Forensic experts examined the scene and collected samples, including fingerprints. Sniffer dogs were also deployed as part of the investigation. Police are examining CCTV footage from the neighbourhood to identify those responsible for the murder. Three people from the locality, including a college student, were taken in for questioning. Police also questioned a man working as a cook for inquiry. Further investigation is underway.

items.title: Bengaluru: No entry for two-wheelers on Electronics City, Airport Road elevated corridors
items.summary: Two-wheelers will soon be barred from two of Bengaluru’s busiest elevated corridors, with the traffic police citing accident risks and congestion. The restrictions will cover the Electronics City and International Airport Rated corridors. They are part of a trial aimed at improving safety and traffic movement. The Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) announced restrictions on five flyovers and elevated corridors after reviewing accident patterns, traffic congestion and problems caused by vehicle breakdowns. Restrictions on the BGS Flyover, Peenya Elevated Corridor, Double-Decker Flyover and International Airport Road Elevated Corridor will begin from September 4. The Electronics City Elevated Corridor too will have these restrictions from September 11. The International Airport Road Elevated Corridor, between Sanjeevnagar Cross and Vidyashilp Junction, will no longer allow two-wheelers or passenger autorickshaws. Goods vehicles of all categories will also be prohibited on the stretch between 6 am and 10 pm. The Electronics City Elevated Corridor will have the most extensive restrictions. From September 11, two-wheelers, passenger autorickshaws and three-wheeler goods autos will be prohibited throughout the day. items.title: Andhra CM announces Rs 10 lakh compensation for families of 8 killed in Palnadu crash
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has announced an ex gratia of Rs 10 lakh each for the families of the eight people who died in a road accident at Chilakaluripet in Palnadu district. He directed officials to provide the assistance to the bereaved families at the earliest. The accident took place in the early hours of August 27 at Addaroad Centre in Chilakaluripet town after a private bus collided with an auto-rickshaw carrying 15 people in Palnadu district. The victims, all residents of Veluru village in Chilakaluripet mandal, were travelling in an auto-rickshaw after attending a birthday celebration. According to the police, the group was returning to Veluru after travelling to Konda Manjuluru village in J Panguluru mandal of Prakasam district. There were 15 people in the auto, including four children, nine women and two men. As the auto-rickshaw was taking a turn at Addaroad Centre, a private travel bus travelling from Vijayawada towards Tirupati collided with it. The impact left several passengers seriously injured. Four people died at the accident spot. Another victim died while undergoing treatment at the Chilakaluripet Government Hospital, while two others later succumbed to their injuries at the Government General Hospital in Guntur. The deceased were identified as Bontha Babu Rao, 62, Bontha Manemma, 55, Bontha Sampurnamma, 70, Choutupalli Laksmamma, 75, Bontha Gangamma, 50, Sowtupalli Suvartha, 45, and Bontha Mariyamma, 45. All seven were residents of Veluru village. The injured were identified as Talluri Venkayamma, 50, Choutupalli Dhanalakshmi, 30, Talluri Abhiram, 6, Choutupalli Subbulu, 60, Bontha Arun Kumar, 40, who was driving the auto, Bontha Samuel Babu, 6, Bontha Pallavi, 12, and Bontha Divya, 7.

Police said the accused was apprehended on the evening of August 30, within 30 hours of receiving the complaint. The room was accessed through a window, where the woman was found dead with injuries. items.title: How does a collapsing glacier turn into a lethal wall of mud and water? An expert explains what happened in Nepal
items.summary: A collapsing glacier in Tibet led to a devastating wall of water and debris roaring through a valley in Nepal , leaving hundreds dead and many hundreds still missing. Stuart Dunning is a professor of applied geomorphology who researches disaster risk reduction in high mountain areas and has closely studied the 2021 Chamoli disaster, a similar event. He’s part of a loose group of 50 or more international experts who come together to pool expertise and provide rapid analysis of events like these. The Conversation asked him about the science behind this event, and what we can expect in future. What exactly happened – and how can a collapsing glacier generate such a powerful flood? The exact sequence of events that sent so much debris and water downstream is something we are still trying to unravel. There are a number of possibilities. One is that a large bedrock landslide took the glacier with it. Another is that a bedrock landslide destabilised the glacier and it fell very shortly after. Another is that the glacier failed first and then the bedrock above failed. I think the best description is that a rock-ice avalanche began at around 4,800 metres and fell over 1,200 metres. There was enough ice in the initial collapse – and perhaps subsequently picked up – that it could generate the water to turn it into a devastating long-runout debris flow. This is far more damaging than a dry rock avalanche. The flow travelled along the river, gaining water. It would have been eroding the valley floor and sides as it went. Further downstream, that material will have been deposited across the landscape. What do we call this event? Is it a glacial outburst flood, a landslide, an ice avalanche… something else? I’m part of a group of 50 or more hazard experts debating what to term this. items.title: Priyank Kharge offers to quit politics if Kumaraswamy proves KPSC scam link
items.summary: Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge on Monday, August 31 challenged Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy to produce evidence linking him to the alleged Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) recruitment scam. The alleged scam is related to irregularities in a test for the appointment of Assistant Executive Engineers (AEE) under the Rural Drinking Water Supply Scheme. Kharge said he was willing to quit politics if there was even “an iota of evidence” establishing his involvement in the alleged irregularities. He also challenged Kumaraswamy to retire from politics if any involvement of the BJP or JD(S) was established in the case. “If my involvement is proven, I am ready to forgo politics entirely. Even my family will not come (to politics),” Kharge told reporters. items.title: Karnataka extends Gruha Jyothi verification deadline by a month to Sept 30
items.summary: The Karnataka government has extended the deadline for the door-to-door verification of Gruha Jyothi scheme beneficiaries by a month, with the survey now set to continue until September 30. The review survey began on July 1, with August 31 being the original deadline. As of May 2026, there were 68.86 lakh Gruha Jyothi beneficiaries across the eight districts under the Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Ltd. (BESCOM). Of these, 46.7 lakh, or about 70%, had been surveyed by August 31. BESCOM Managing Director N Shivashankara has urged the remaining beneficiaries to cooperate with meter readers and provide the required documents when officials visit their homes from September 1. According to BESCOM officials, some beneficiaries living in apartments in Bengaluru had not been cooperating with survey staff. Apartment residents have been asked to facilitate access for officials visiting their premises. For locked houses, meter readers will make up to three visits at different times. During each visit, they will record the latitude and longitude of the premises and mark the property as “DL” (door lock) on the mobile app. Once a house is marked as locked, an SMS with the meter reader’s name and contact number will be sent to the beneficiary’s registered mobile number. This will be done up to three times, allowing beneficiaries to contact the meter reader and complete the verification. For vacant premises, staff must physically visit the location and record its latitude and longitude before marking it as “VACANT” and registering it on the app. Beneficiaries seeking assistance with the survey can contact the BESCOM helpline numbers 9480816111, 9480816112, 9480816113 or 9480816114.

items.summary: Argentina superstar Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international soccer on Monday, ending 21 years of national-team duty that were capped by winning the World Cup in 2022 to secure his place in the pantheon of the game's greatest ever players. "It was a decision that hurt — and still hurts deeply — but I understand that the time has come," the 39-year-old Messi said on his Instagram account. Messi, who will continue to play at club level with Inter Miami in Major League Soccer, played in a record-tying six World Cups. He won it four years ago in a tournament he dominated in Qatar and also led Argentina to the title match in 2014 and again this year, when the Albiceleste lost to Spain in extra time in New Jersey. Messi stands shoulder to shoulder with Diego Maradona, a compatriot with whom he was so often compared, and Brazil icon Pelé as the greatest players of all time. For many, he's the best. "I swear to you that I always gave it my all — not just in these last few years when we won everything, but before that too," Messi wrote. "I always fought and left everything on the field for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football." Messi played 207 games for Argentina and finishes as its all-time leading scorer with 125 goals, 21 of them in World Cups. Only one player has more goals in men's internationals — his long-time rival Cristiano Ronaldo, who has 146 and has yet to announce his retirement from Portugal duty.
